about.label: MONUMENT ATLAS / FIELD NOTES
about.title: A monument in layers.
about.footnote: An independent architectural exploration. Not affiliated with the archaeological park.
about.summary: Compare the present-day ruins with a plausible ancient reconstruction. Both share an approximate 189 × 156 metre footprint and a 48 metre outer wall. The ancient form does not represent one precise historical date.
about.evidence: The surviving exterior guides the complete arcades and attic. The archaeological park documents marble seating, red-and-white plaster in passages, and an arena floor above the underground machinery. Exhibition models inform the seating bowl and upper colonnade.
about.interpretation: The exact seat count, stair and ramp routes, timber upper seats, mast dimensions, colors and decorative profiles are simplified interpretations. The awning fabric is shown stowed. Statues, painted figures, all underground rooms, and the surrounding city are outside this study. In the ruins, the arena platform and visitor routes remain approximate.

help.label: FIND YOUR WAY
help.title: Take a closer look.
help.orbit: Drag with one finger or the left mouse button.
help.zoom: Scroll, pinch, or use the + and − buttons.

help.walk: Drag to look. Use WASD or the arrow pad to walk. Shift moves faster. Follow the entrance passage to the arena and its walkways.
help.view: Choose any of the four perspectives. On foot, these take you to a safe starting position.
help.reset: Press R to reset the current view. Escape exits walking. Use the overview button to return to orbit.

wall.label: 01 / TRAVERTINE & TIME
wall.title: The surviving outer wall
wall.text: Three arcaded storeys and a windowed attic rise along the northern side. Much of the southern outer wall is lost, exposing the inner structure. Brick buttresses support the surviving ends.
wall.learn: Learn about the surviving outer wall

hypogeum.label: 02 / BELOW THE ARENA
hypogeum.title: The hypogeum
hypogeum.text: The arena floor once concealed a network of corridors, lifts, and holding spaces. Its exposed brick walls now reveal the infrastructure behind the spectacles. This study simplifies the underground layout.

cavea.label: 03 / THE CAVEA
cavea.title: The seating terraces
cavea.text: Concentric tiers once carried the audience high above the arena. Most original seats are gone; broken masonry, radial supports, and a small preserved seating section reveal the former arrangement.

wall.label: 01 / THE COMPLETE EXTERIOR
wall.title: The restored outer wall
wall.text: Eighty bays form an elliptical enclosure. Three arcaded storeys support a windowed attic. Wooden masts suggest the awning system; its fabric is stowed in this interpretation.
wall.learn: Learn about the restored outer wall

hypogeum.label: 02 / THE ARENA FLOOR
hypogeum.title: A covered arena
hypogeum.text: The sand-covered arena conceals the underground stage machinery. Archaeological evidence supports a covered floor. Its exact construction and the entrance ramps are simplified here.

cavea.label: 03 / THE CAVEA
cavea.title: The complete seating bowl
cavea.text: Marble seats, radial aisles and an upper colonnade restore the bowl. The row count, timber upper seats, stair routes, colors and decorative details are interpretations. This model does not represent one precise historical date.
